title: Skill-bank rotation and slice triage canvas
creator: Asha Raman
description: Problem: We repeatedly over- or under-allocate specialized skills (e.g., inference performance, infra reliability, console UX) across product cycles which forces scope churn mid-cycle. Objective: Create a lightweight, repeatable Skill Bank + Slice Triage Canvas process that lets PMs and Eng leads build staffing plans that are robust to small staffing churn and objectively prioritize slices for delivery. Scope: 1) Define Skill Bank taxonomy and rotation rules, 2) Build a Slice Triage Canvas template to score and bucket work, 3) Run 3 staffing simulations (baseline, 15% person-days lost, rapid surge) and produce a recommended tranche plan for the upcoming cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Skill Bank taxonomy documented and shared as a single-page sheet (roles, grade, primary/secondary skills)
Slice Triage Canvas template available in Drive and a completed example for the runtime-1.18 initiative
Three staffing simulations completed with assumptions captured and results summarized in the capacity-sim dashboard
PM + Eng leadership sign-off on the tranche recommendation and reserve lanes
Playbook steps added to the cycle-planning checklist (docs and 1-pager)
Handoff notes for rotational staffing created and committed to the Cycle Confluence page
discussion: Notes from initial workshop (2025-11-05): We agreed that current planning happens too late and lacks a clear tie between OKR priorities and the skill set required to deliver them. Diego proposed a Skill Bank where each role entry includes 3 tags: primary competency, backup competency, and bench availability (fraction of time available for rotation). Asha suggested immediate guardrails: a single dedicated core lane, one surge lane, and a small floating reserve to cover bus-factor events. Trade-offs discussed: tighter gating increases planning overhead but reduces mid-cycle breaks; looser rules preserve autonomy but increase scope churn. We debated metrics for scoring slices: customer impact, regression risk, infra cost delta, and delivery complexity. Decided to weight customer impact highest for this cycle due to upcoming enterprise trials.
decisions: Adopt three-lane staffing model: Core (committed), Surge (conditional commits), Reserve (floating, <10% capacity)
Slice Triage Canvas will use a 4-factor score (Impact=40%, Risk=25%, Complexity=20%, Cost delta=15%) to bucket work into Minimal/Stretch/Defer
Run Monte Carlo simulation for 1,000 iterations across three scenarios to estimate probability of meeting core MVs
Require each tranche to list explicit cross-training tasks and a named backup for every core skill slot

notes_for_engineering: Eng teams should provide one representative to validate skill mappings and nominate backups. The simulation assumes uniform productivity; if your team runs with large variance (e.g., single senior contributor owning kernel work), flag that as a special constraint in the Canvas.
